## 1. Lagos Real Fake Life
This vibrant Nollywood comedy, directed by Mike Ezuruonye, hilariously skewers the aspirational, often fabricated, lifestyles paraded by some residents of Lagos. It’s a sharp, funny look at social media personas and the pressure to keep up appearances, offering both laughter and a touch of social commentary.

## 2. The Accidental Spy
Ramsey Nouah stars as a celebrated Nollywood actor forced to confront his imposter in this thrilling drama. Following a year-long hiatus, his quest for justice takes him on a suspenseful journey, showcasing the star power of Nouah and the intricate storytelling of director Moses Inwang.

## 3. Payday
While specific details are scarce, "Payday" joins "Lagos Real Fake Life" and "The Accidental Spy" as part of a fresh wave of Nigerian cinema hitting Netflix. These additions promise authentic storytelling and a glimpse into contemporary Nigerian culture, offering a welcome alternative to mainstream Hollywood fare.

## 4. Murder Mystery
Adam Sandler and Jennifer Aniston reunite for this wildly popular Netflix original comedy. The film garnered massive viewership, proving its status as a go-to comfort watch that delivers reliable laughs and a breezy international caper that millions have already enjoyed.

## 5. Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes
For fans of epic sci-fi sagas, this latest installment in the "Planet of the Apes" franchise offers a visually stunning continuation of the ape-led world. It expands the lore with new characters and challenges, making it a compelling watch for both long-time fans and newcomers curious about this post-human future.

## 6. Elizabeth Taylor Documentary (Title Not Specified)
While the specific title isn't listed, the presence of an Elizabeth Taylor documentary on a major streaming platform signals an opportunity to delve into the life of a true Hollywood icon. Expect behind-the-scenes glamour, personal struggles, and the enduring legacy of a cinematic legend.

## 7. A Surprise Nollywood Gem (Placeholder)
With the influx of new Nigerian films like "Lagos Real Fake Life" and "The Accidental Spy," there's always a chance for another standout title to emerge. Keep an eye out for unexpected narratives that showcase the dynamism and growing global influence of Nollywood cinema.
Bottom Line: This weekend's Netflix lineup is a diverse mix, blending Nigerian storytelling with Hollywood blockbusters and insightful documentaries for a rich viewing experience.

content_raw: Who will take the box office crown from Johnny Depp and Ti West ’s Ebenezer ? The Hollywood veteran's comeback following off-screen controversy proved hugely popular last weekend, as the Charles Dickens adaptation topped the box office charts and exceeded most expectations. But a little-known fantasy franchise looks set to take the box office throne, as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping finally makes its big-screen debut. The latest adaptation from Suzanne Collins ' massively popular series of books might be at the top of your watchlist, but don't let it distract you from the plethora of options available from the comfort of your own home. Here's a look at three movies you should watch this weekend on Netflix .
